proposals.note: Designed a translation-invariant ansatz block using a ring topology of CNOTs and site-specific parameterized rotations (RZ and RY). The block structure is invariant under cyclic permutation of qubits (generator [1,2,3,4,5,0]), assuming the parameters p0..p5 are permuted accordingly. This symmetry aligns with the periodic nature of the input domain [0, 2pi) and the likely cyclic structure of the underlying analytic function, potentially improving generalization and reducing effective parameter space complexity. The block uses 24 gates and 6 trainable parameters.

proposals.note: Entangling layer with linear connectivity (CNOT chain) and periodic boundary condition (CNOT 5->0) to capture cyclic dependencies in the 6-site input. Structure: RZ layer (phase encoding) -> Entangling -> RY layer (basis rotation) -> Entangling. This is a standard hardware-efficient ansatz block (Strongly Entangling Layers) which provides high expressibility for regression tasks on 6 qubits. The use of CNOTs ensures strong entanglement propagation across all qubits, while the RZ/RY layers allow for arbitrary single-qubit rotations. The periodic connection helps if the underlying analytic formula has cyclic symmetry, but even without it, it improves connectivity compared to a linear chain.

This structure provides sufficient expressivity to model complex relationships between the 6 input features and the 2 targets, leveraging the data re-uploading feature map. The use of 6 parameters (one per qubit) allows for local rotations while the CNOTs entangle neighboring qubits. This design is robust and avoids the pitfalls of the previous hypothesis which failed due to incorrect symmetry assumptions.

proposals.note: Designed a translation-invariant ansatz block to exploit the cyclic symmetry of the 6-site ring topology implied by the input indexing. The block consists of uniform single-qubit rotations (RY, RZ) followed by a full cycle of CNOTs. Parameters are tied across all sites (p0 for RY, p1 for RZ) to enforce permutation invariance under the cyclic shift generator (0->1->...->5->0). This structure reduces the parameter count significantly compared to unconstrained blocks, potentially improving generalization and training stability for regression tasks on structured data, while maintaining sufficient entanglement depth via the CNOT cycles.
